# Search recipes by ingredients

## Problem Statement

Registered home cooks often decide what to make based on what is already in the fridge, not on a dish name. Right now the recipe site can only be searched by recipe title, so a cook who has leeks and potatoes has to guess dish names until one matches, and may give up before finding a recipe they could cook. In a survey of 400 registered users, 61 percent said they want to search by the ingredients they have. This affects registered cooks searching on a phone or on a computer.

## Business Alignment

**Job to Be Done:** When I have a few ingredients at home and no dish in mind, I want to type those ingredients into the recipe site's search, so I can find a published recipe that uses all of them without guessing dish names.

**Impact Map:**
- **Goal:** Let registered home cooks find recipes starting from the ingredients they have. This is the need 61 percent of 400 surveyed registered users asked for (parent vision, Problem Statement).
- **Actor:** A registered home cook searching the recipe site on a phone or a computer (parent vision, Target Audience).
- **Impact:** The cook enters the ingredients they have and reaches a recipe that uses all of them, either straight from the results or after one edit following a no-match message, instead of guessing dish titles.
- **Deliverable:** Ingredient search on the existing search page. It takes 1 to 5 English ingredient names, lists the published recipes that use all of them, answers within 2 seconds for 95 percent of searches, and shows a no-match message that suggests removing one ingredient.

**Alignment checks:**
- The Goal traces to the vision's problem statement: YES
- The Actor is the vision's target audience: YES
- The Impact is an observable change in behavior (searching by ingredient instead of guessing titles): YES
- The Deliverable covers a single functional area (ingredient search on one page): YES

**Overlap check:** There are no sibling stubs. Glob `plans/functional/find-recipes-by-ingredient-*.md` matched only this file.

## User Stories

**Story 1.** **As a** registered home cook, **I want** to enter up to five ingredients I have and see the published recipes that use all of them, **so that** I can choose a dish from what is in my fridge without guessing dish names. (Scenarios 1–5)

**Story 2.** **As a** registered home cook searching on a phone or a computer, **I want** ingredient search on the search page I already use to answer within 2 seconds, **so that** I can decide what to cook without waiting and can still find recipes by title as before. (Scenarios 6–8)

**Story 3.** **As a** registered home cook whose ingredients match no recipe, **I want** to be told so and shown what to change, **so that** I can widen my search and still reach a recipe instead of hitting a dead end. (Scenarios 9–11)

Stories 2 and 3 build on the search from Story 1. All three are delivered in this one plan, so none of them needs a separate `depends_on`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Scenario 1: Recipes that use all entered ingredients are shown**
  Given the published recipes "Leek and potato soup" (leeks, potatoes, vegetable stock) and "Potato gratin" (potatoes, cream, cheese)
  When a registered cook searches with the ingredients "leeks" and "potatoes"
  Then "Leek and potato soup" appears in the results
  And "Potato gratin" does not appear in the results

- [ ] **Scenario 2: Unpublished recipes are never shown**
  Given an unpublished draft recipe whose ingredients include leeks and potatoes
  When a registered cook searches with "leeks" and "potatoes"
  Then the draft recipe does not appear in the results

- [ ] **Scenario 3: Letter case and singular or plural do not matter**
  Given a published recipe whose ingredient list names "Leek" and "potato"
  When a registered cook searches with "LEEKS" and "Potatoes"
  Then that recipe appears in the results

- [ ] **Scenario 4: An entered name matches a longer ingredient name that contains it as whole words**
  Given a published recipe whose ingredient list names "chicken thighs" and "rice"
  When a registered cook searches with "chicken" and "rice"
  Then that recipe appears in the results
  And searching with "chick" and "rice" does not return that recipe, because part of a word does not match

- [ ] **Scenario 5: A sixth ingredient is refused**
  Given a registered cook who has entered five ingredients
  When they try to add a sixth ingredient
  Then the sixth ingredient is not added
  And the page shows a message that a search takes at most 5 ingredients
  And the five ingredients already entered stay in place

- [ ] **Scenario 6: 95 percent of searches answer within 2 seconds**
  Given the full catalogue of published recipes
  When 1,000 ingredient searches, each with 1 to 5 ingredients, are submitted on the search page
  Then at least 950 of them show their results, or the no-match message, within 2 seconds of being submitted

- [ ] **Scenario 7: Ingredient search works on a phone screen**
  Given a registered cook using the search page on a phone screen 375 pixels wide
  When they enter five ingredients and search
  Then the five entered ingredients and the results fit the screen width, so nothing needs scrolling sideways

- [ ] **Scenario 8: Title search is unchanged**
  Given 20 searches by recipe title, and the recipes each one returned, recorded before ingredient search is added
  When the same 20 title searches are run after ingredient search is added
  Then each one returns the same recipes as before

- [ ] **Scenario 9: No recipe uses all the ingredients**
  Given that no published recipe uses all of "leeks", "potatoes" and "mango", while each of the three is used by at least one published recipe
  When a registered cook searches with those three ingredients
  Then the page shows a message saying that no recipe uses all three ingredients
  And the message suggests removing one ingredient
  And the three entered ingredients stay on the page

- [ ] **Scenario 10: Removing one ingredient shows results for the rest**
  Given a cook who got the no-match message for "leeks", "potatoes" and "mango"
  And a published recipe that uses leeks and potatoes
  When the cook removes "mango"
  Then the results for "leeks" and "potatoes" are shown without the cook retyping them
  And that recipe appears in the results

- [ ] **Scenario 11: A single ingredient that matches nothing**
  Given that no published recipe uses "saffron"
  When a registered cook searches with "saffron" as the only ingredient
  Then the page shows a message saying that no recipe uses "saffron"
  And the message suggests trying a different ingredient instead of removing one

## Scope

### In Scope
- Ingredient search on the existing search page, taking 1 to 5 ingredient names in English per search (Scenarios 1 and 5)
- Results that list only published recipes that use every ingredient entered (Scenarios 1 and 2)
- A match rule that ignores letter case, treats the singular and plural of an English name as the same, and matches an entered name that appears as whole words inside a recipe's ingredient name (Scenarios 3 and 4)
- Results, or the no-match message, shown within 2 seconds of submitting for at least 95 percent of searches (Scenario 6)
- Ingredient entry and results usable on a phone screen 375 pixels wide and on a computer (Scenario 7)
- Search by recipe title on the same page returns the same results as before this change (Scenario 8)
- A no-match message that suggests removing one ingredient, and a separate message for a single ingredient that matches nothing (Scenarios 9 and 11)
- Removing an entered ingredient runs the search again with the remaining ingredients (Scenario 10)

### Out of Scope
- Searching by dish name: this already exists. The parent vision excludes it; this plan only requires that it keeps returning the same results (Scenario 8).
- Dietary filters: excluded by the parent vision's scope.
- Ingredient names in languages other than English: excluded by the parent vision's scope.

## Risks

### Technical Risks
- **Search speed**: Finding the recipes that use all of up to five ingredients, under the case, singular/plural and whole-word match rule, across the full published catalogue may take longer than 2 seconds for more than 5 percent of searches. This plan does not know how big the catalogue is or how recipes store their ingredients, because this repository holds no recipe-site code: Glob `**/*` over the project root matched 4 files, all of them plans, a status file or an agent definition.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH (missing the budget could mean reworking how ingredients are stored or indexed)
  - Mitigation: Spike: run 1,000 searches of 1 to 5 ingredients against a copy of the full published catalogue before the implementation plan settles on a design.
- **Form of the ingredient data**: If recipes keep ingredients as free-text lines such as "2 large leeks, sliced" rather than as ingredient names, matching "leeks" requires pulling the name out of each line, and recipes with unusual wording will be missed.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Sample 100 published recipes and check how their ingredient lists are written before the implementation plan is drafted.
- **Title search breaking**: Adding ingredient search to the existing search page could change what title searches return.
  - Likelihood: LOW
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Record 20 title searches and their results before the change, then re-run them after it (Scenario 8).

### Business Risks
- **Generic no-match suggestion (a documented choice)**: This plan follows the vision's wording, so the message suggests removing one ingredient without naming which one. Naming the ingredient whose removal brings recipes back is a different build: up to five extra searches inside the same 2-second budget.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM (cooks may not know which ingredient to drop)
  - Impact: LOW
  - Mitigation: Review this choice with the owner at Gate 1. The alternative is to name the ingredient to remove.
- **Whole-word match rule (a documented choice)**: "potato" also finds a recipe that lists "sweet potato", because the rule matches an entered name that appears as whole words in a longer name. Without the rule, "chicken" would not find "chicken thighs".
  - Likelihood: HIGH (it follows directly from the rule)
  - Impact: LOW
  - Mitigation: Review the rule with the owner at Gate 1, using the examples "chicken" → "chicken thighs" and "potato" → "sweet potato".
- **Who may search (a documented choice)**: The vision names registered cooks as the audience but does not say whether signed-out visitors may use ingredient search. This plan gives ingredient search the same access as the existing title search.
  - Likelihood: LOW
  - Impact: LOW
  - Mitigation: Confirm with the owner at Gate 1.

### Dependency Risks
- **Existing search page and recipe records**: This plan builds on the existing search page and on two things every existing recipe must have: a published status and an ingredient list. Neither is in this repository (same Glob as above), so this plan has not checked that they exist in the form it needs. `depends_on` is "none", and the vision has no other stub.
  - Likelihood: LOW
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Locate the code for the search page and for recipe storage, and confirm both, before the implementation plan is drafted.

## Priority

**Priority: HIGH** (Score: 7/9)
- Dependency: MEDIUM (2) -- this is the only stub from this vision, so no other stub depends on it and it depends on none
- Business Impact: HIGH (3) -- it delivers the vision's whole primary goal, which 61 percent of 400 surveyed registered users asked for
- Technical Risk: MEDIUM (2) -- matching all of up to five ingredients within 2 seconds is of moderate complexity; no new technology is involved, but the form of the recipe data has not been checked
